# Description

> ## ⛔ DO NOT POST THIS ONE YET

> this one has stop conditions.

## Business context / goal

A MaidVisa client's monthly payment is the maid's salary plus the WPS processing fee. When a month's payment never arrives, or arrives short of the contract's own agreed amount, with no replacement settling it and nobody chasing, the money is simply not collected.

This check scores every in-scope contract-month against what the contract says was owed.

**Expected outcome:** an uncollected or short MaidVisa monthly payment is surfaced per contract-month, at the shortfall amount, with the evidence behind it.

An AI verifier reads the account record behind each red flag and returns an advisory verdict. The verdict never changes a case's state; only a human closes a case.

## Deployment readiness — four blockers

1. ⛔ **Stage 0 is marked UNTESTED by its own author** and its sticky note says: *"Do not run it until someone confirms clientmgmt is healthy, and re-measure the real per-page cost first."*
2. ⛔ **Stage 0 exists because this check caused a production outage.** On 2026-08-19 a sweep of ~116 requests took the whole `clientmgmt` module to nginx 503 — contract search *and* get-client-details, even at `size=1`. See `INCIDENT-2026-08-19-clientmgmt-503.md`. The rebuild has never been run against a healthy module.
3. ⛔ **Stages 1 and 0 still call `/clientmgmt/contract/search/page`** — on the route ban, and the endpoint implicated in that outage. Stage 2's ledger call was swapped to `/accounting/payments/search` on 2026-08-27; the contract-search side was deliberately **not** swapped, because Stage 1 uses it as a *counter* (`size=1`, read `totalElements`) and no replacement is a count endpoint, and Stage 0's two-pass pager is built around its 40-row page-0 cap. That is a rebuild, not a swap.
4. ⚠ **Stage 3's `Rollup In` webhook had no authentication of any kind until 2026-08-25.** It now checks a shared secret, but the live slot is a short literal held inline in a Code node. Move it to an `httpHeaderAuth` credential before this is reachable from production.

**Recommendation: hold this ticket until 1–3 are resolved.** The other five checks in this batch can proceed independently.

## Trigger & schedule

**Scheduled.** Monthly, on the 15th at 06:00 Asia/Dubai. Each run audits the *previous full calendar month* — payments need time to settle, so the two-week lag is deliberate.

No webhook, no manual trigger, no inbound endpoint of any kind.

> **PRE-DEPLOYMENT CONVERSION REQUIRED — two webhooks to remove.** Stage 1's entry is a webhook (`Run Check`) and must become the schedule trigger. Stage 3 additionally exposes `POST /mv-monthly-payment-rollup`, which is deleted.
>
> **Deleting the rollup entry has a stated cost.** It exists because a run can die mid-slice and everything already scored would otherwise be unreportable — Stage 1 is the only other way in and it always sweeps the ERP first. The replacement is a **manual execution of Stage 3** for a dead run. That is acceptable, but it must be a documented fallback rather than a capability that silently disappears.
